statement: The cumulative frequency table shows the finishing times of the $80$ runners in a $5$-kilometer race. Each entry gives the number of runners who finished in less than the given time. $$\begin{array}{c|c} \text{Finishing time} & \text{Number of runners} \\ \hline \text{Less than } 20 \text{ minutes} & 6 \\ \text{Less than } 25 \text{ minutes} & 22 \\ \text{Less than } 30 \text{ minutes} & 47 \\ \text{Less than } 35 \text{ minutes} & 68 \\ \text{Less than } 40 \text{ minutes} & 80 \end{array}$$ What percent of the runners finished in at least $25$ minutes but less than $35$ minutes?

choices.misconception: I used only the runners from 30 to less than 35 minutes, 68 minus 47, which is 21, and divided by 80.
I used only the runners from 25 to less than 30 minutes, 47 minus 22, which is 25, and divided by 80.
I correctly found 46 runners in the time window but wrote 46 as the percent without dividing by 80.

hints: Each row counts all runners below that time, including the ones counted in earlier rows.
Runners with times from $25$ up to $35$ minutes are the ones under $35$ minutes who are not under $25$ minutes.
That is $68 - 22 = 46$ runners. Now turn $46$ out of $80$ into a percent.

solutions.reliable: The number of runners under $35$ minutes is $68$, and $22$ of them were under $25$ minutes. So $68 - 22 = 46$ runners finished in at least $25$ but less than $35$ minutes. As a percent of all runners, that is $\dfrac{46}{80} = 0.575 = 57.5\%$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
